title: THE OLYMPIC · CHAIN & CLIMB
vibe: GREEN · You said bring it, and you're fresh off a full rest day — so today is the heaviest, most athletic thing in your library that you have never actually run: the double-bell Olympic chain. Clean, front squat, jerk, both 40s, and the bells do not touch the ground until the round is over. Then you climb a hill instead of running another flat two-miler. Grip, lungs and legs all get a vote. Eight rounds is the target — go get them.
why: Two things drove today. First, you're genuinely fresh: a full rest day yesterday, no soreness, 7h sleep, and you told me to bring it — that is the exact readiness profile you save for explosive, heavy, technical work, and it would be a waste to spend it on another pump or another isolation day. Second, the log has two real holes. Explosive ballistic power hasn't been touched since 07-18/07-19 (double swings and the Tabata), making it your most neglected quality by a wide margin. And the complex/chain shape — a sequence of lifts done unbroken with the bells never resting — has literally never been run in your log; you started one on 07-13 and got interrupted 14 days ago. So today closes both at once with Neupert's Olympic chain: double clean (ballistic pull) into double front squat (leg strength) into double jerk (explosive overhead push), 80 lb, no rest inside the round. Your wildcard is the jerk itself — the double dip under the bells — which has never appeared once in this log; today's research lens was hardstyle/girevoy long cycle, and the consistent advice there is to build in timed sets, groove the dip first, and let the chain be the conditioning. On the run: you set a NEW 2-mile PR Saturday, 15:06 with a 7:34/7:24 negative split, on a day I'd deliberately prescribed no treadmill at all. Message received — I stopped writing 'no run' plans. But you have nothing to prove on the flat two days after a PR, so today's run is a 12-minute incline pyramid climbing to 12%. Same heart rate, roughly half the pounding, and it hits the one lever that actually protects the connective tissue that is your only real risk at 250 lb. Core rotates off Saturday's ab flexion to overhead and anti-extension work, which also brings the get-up back after eight days away.

blocks.title: MOBILITY WARM-UP · FLOW + FRONT RACK
blocks.meta: ~7 min · Moves Method Day C (continuous flow) + rack/overhead prep · matches a day built on unbroken chains
blocks.text: Today's warm-up is a FLOW, not a checklist — one continuous moving sequence, which is the same idea as the session itself. Move for ~3 min without stopping: rock-backs x8 · cross-crawls 10/side · dead-bug reach 5/side · baby crawl forward and back 20 steps · a few slow rolls side to side · segmental cat-cow x5. Keep it linked, breathe through your nose, no pauses. Then ~4 min of specific prep for the front rack and the overhead position you're about to load hard: shoulder dislocates (towel or broomstick) x10 · thoracic rotations 8/side · ankle rocks in a deep squat 10/side (you need dorsiflexion to catch a double front squat) · wrist rocks and circles 15 (the rack sits on your forearms) · lat and tricep overhead reach 20s/side. Finish with the rehearsal: 3 slow chains with ONE 40 — clean, front squat, press — just to wake the pattern up. Do not skip the ankle and wrist work; those two are what let the rack feel comfortable instead of like a fight.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · THE OLYMPIC (double-bell chain)
blocks.meta: ~18 min clock · 2×40 lb (80 lb total) · clean → front squat → jerk, unbroken · RPE 8 · THE session
blocks.format: COMPLEX / CHAIN · 18-min clock · 1 round = 3 double cleans + 3 double front squats + 3 double jerks with the bells NEVER touching the ground · rest 60–75s between rounds · GREEN target 8 rounds · YELLOW 6
blocks.workRest: Clean both bells to the rack and everything after that happens without setting them down. Three cleans, straight into three front squats, straight into three jerks, then park them and rest 60 to 75 seconds. That is one round. The bells hitting the floor before you finish the chain means the round is over — that is the whole discipline of a complex, and it is why this feels nothing like your usual station work. Rounds 1–2 use a PUSH PRESS so you can groove the dip and drive; from round 3 on, switch to the full JERK (the second dip under the bells) — that is today's wildcard and it is the piece you have never done in this log. Count rounds, not minutes.

items.name: 1 · Double Clean ×3
items.detail: 2×40 lb · hike the bells back between your legs and snap the hips to float them into the rack — this is a HINGE that ends in a rack position, not a curl. Let the bells roll around your forearms, don't bang your wrists. Elbows down and into the ribs, bells resting on the forearm, standing tall. This is your ballistic pull and it's the pattern that's been missing for over a week.

items.name: 2 · Double Front Squat ×3
items.detail: 2×40 lb from the rack · elbows stay tight to the body, chest up, sit straight down between your heels to full depth, drive up through mid-foot. The load pulls you forward — brace hard and fight it. You did 5×5 of these on 07-18 so the weight is known; the difference today is you arrive already breathing from the cleans.

items.name: 3 · Double Jerk ×3 (WILDCARD)
items.detail: 2×40 lb from the rack · dip a few inches with a vertical torso, drive explosively through the legs, and as the bells travel up DIP UNDER them a second time to catch them locked out overhead — then stand up. That second dip is what makes it a jerk instead of a push press, and it lets your legs move a load your shoulders alone couldn't. Lock the elbows, bells stacked over the shoulders, ribs down. Rounds 1–2: push press only (no second dip) to warm the pattern. Rounds 3+: full jerk.

blocks.text: This is the main event and the reason today exists. A complex is a different animal from your usual blocks — you don't get to put the weight down and shake your arms out between movements, so grip, breathing and rack tolerance become the limiter alongside the muscles. Nine reps at 80 lb per round doesn't sound like much until round five. The hardstyle and girevoy sources are consistent on how to run this: keep the sets short, keep the rest honest, groove the dip before you chase the jerk, and let the chain supply the conditioning rather than bolting a metcon onto the end. Eight rounds in 18 minutes is your GREEN target and it's an aggressive one. If the rack starts to burn out before your legs do, that's normal and it's the point — that's the part of you this session is actually training. If a round breaks down technically, stop that round, rest, and start the next one clean.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · THE CLIMB (incline pyramid)
blocks.meta: ~12 min · treadmill · speed HELD at 6.0 mph the whole time · incline does all the work: 3% → 6% → 9% → 12% → 9% → 6%
blocks.format: INCLINE PYRAMID · 12 min continuous · six 2-min stages · speed constant, only the grade changes
blocks.workRest: Set the belt to 6.0 mph and leave it there for all twelve minutes. The only thing you touch is the incline. 0:00–2:00 at 3% · 2:00–4:00 at 6% · 4:00–6:00 at 9% · 6:00–8:00 at 12% (the peak, and it will be genuinely hard) · 8:00–10:00 back to 9% · 10:00–12:00 at 6%. Run tall, short quick steps, and cue a CADENCE of about 168–172 — you naturally run around 160, and shortening the stride is the single cheapest thing you can do to cut the impact force going through your joints at 250 lb. Do not hold the rails on the 12% stage.

items.name: Stages 1–3 · Build
items.detail: 6.0 mph at 3%, then 6%, then 9% · two minutes each. Breathing should get noticeably heavier at 9%. Stay tall, don't lean into the belt, quick feet.

items.name: Stage 4 · The Peak
items.detail: 6.0 mph at 12% for two full minutes. This is the hard part of the run. Expect your heart rate to land somewhere near 150–160, which is right where your two-mile tempo puts you — same cardiovascular hit, a fraction of the joint cost. Hands off the rails, drive the knees.

items.name: Stages 5–6 · Descend
items.detail: Back to 9% for two minutes, then 6% for two. Don't let the pace sag as the grade drops — this is where the aerobic work happens once the peak has already put you in the hole.

blocks.text: You set a new 2-mile best on Saturday: 15:06, splits of 7:34 and 7:24, negative again, and you did it on a day the plan explicitly had no treadmill in it. So I'm not writing 'no run' or 'keep it easy' anymore — you're going to run, so the job is choosing the RIGHT run. Two days after a PR you have nothing to gain from a sixth flat two-miler, and flat tempo running is where all your impact comes from. Incline gives you the same heart rate for far fewer and far gentler foot strikes, which directly protects the connective tissue that is the only genuine risk in your training right now. Your engine has never been the limiter — your HR barely reaches 90% of max and your times keep dropping — so today the run gets harder in a way your knees and Achilles don't have to pay for. Steady easy Zone 2 is still the one gap you never fill; if you want a bonus, it's an easy 20-minute jog on a light day, not today.

blocks.title: CORE · OVERHEAD & ANTI-EXTENSION
blocks.meta: ~8 min · 16 kg + one 40 · 3 rounds · brings the get-up back after 8 days
blocks.format: 3 ROUNDS · minimal rest between moves · rest ~45s between rounds
blocks.workRest: Your last three core sessions were anti-rotation, then loaded rotation, then straight ab flexion on Saturday. The one thing missing is holding a load OVERHEAD while refusing to let your back arch — which also happens to be exactly what the jerks demanded of you an hour earlier. Ribs down, glutes on, do not let the lower back hyperextend to hold the weight up.

items.name: Half Get-Up
items.detail: 16 kg · 3/side · from your back, punch the bell up, roll to the elbow, then to the hand, and back down under control. Eyes on the bell. Stop at the hand — no need to stand up. The get-up hasn't been in your training since 07-19, and it's the best midline-under-overhead-load exercise you own.

items.name: Overhead Carry March
items.detail: one 40 lb bell locked out overhead · 30s/side · march in place or walk it, elbow locked, bicep by the ear, ribs pulled DOWN. Every step is your midline preventing your back from arching. Your grip will already be smoked from the chain — that's fine, that's part of it.

items.name: Hardstyle Plank
items.detail: bodyweight · 20–30s · not a long easy plank — squeeze everything as hard as you physically can (glutes, quads, abs, fists) and breathe short and sharp. Maximum tension, short duration. Quality over the clock.

blocks.text: Overhead and anti-extension midline work, which is the pattern your core hasn't seen recently and the one that reinforces today's jerks. The get-up is back after more than a week away, the overhead carry loads the midline in the exact position the jerk finishes in, and the hardstyle plank teaches maximum full-body tension in twenty hard seconds. Three rounds and you're done.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN
blocks.meta: ~4 min · calves and hip flexors from the hill, lats and rack from the chain
blocks.text: Walk it out at 3.0 mph, 0% for 60s to let the heart rate come down. Then: calf and Achilles stretch 40s/side against the wall (the 12% grade loaded those hard — do not skip this one) · half-kneeling hip flexor stretch 30s/side · overhead lat and tricep stretch 30s/side · doorway or floor pec stretch 30s/side to open what the rack position closed · wrist flexor stretch 20s each · 5 slow nasal breaths lying on your back. Report back with FOUR things: how many rounds of the Olympic chain you finished, how the double JERK felt (particularly whether you found the second dip or ended up push-pressing it), your heart rate at the 12% peak of the climb, and whether the grip or the lungs gave out first. That last one tells me whether to load the next chain heavier or make it longer.

timer.emomUnit: No EMOM today. Block 1 = an 18-minute COUNTDOWN — run chains and rest 60–75s, count rounds (target 8). Block 2 = a 12-minute COUNTDOWN, change the incline every 2 minutes. Block 3 = 3 rounds by feel. Use the countdown timer for the two clocked blocks and ignore it everywhere else.
